# 2026-10-09 — Local 30-year ballpark run (synthetic, not CI)
**Status:** CALCULATED / NON-CANON / ZERO REALIZED CREDIT. Result generated by a local faithful Python reproduction of the committed `gypsum_allocation.py` allocation logic; GitHub branch source not directly executed by CI. Inputs are entirely hypothetical; soil quality and industrial acceptance are toggled true **for sensitivity only**, NOT measured approvals. Actual national imports are not displaced by this calculation.
## Three scenarios
| Scenario | Annual assumed qualified dry gypsum | Synthetic eligible sodic hectares | Initial reclamation gypsum t/ha | Yearly decline | Ongoing t/ha/y | Sulfur-shortfall AGR cap | acid conversion t/t | 30y AGR gypsum | 30y possible acid | Y30 AGR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LOW | 30,000t | 500 | 10 | 30% | 0.1 | 25% | 0.35 | 17,696t | 308,806t | 50t |
| BASE | 70,000t | 2,000 | 20 | 20% | 0.3 | 40% | 0.40 | 179,325t | 768,270t | 600t |
| HIGH | 110,000t | 5,000 | 30 | 12% | 0.5 | 50% | 0.45 | 594,972t | 1,217,263t | 2,500t |

All three have 0 modeled closing inventory **only because simulated industrial qualification is set true and the hub is assumed able to absorb the remainder**, not because hub capacity exists. Year 1 agriculture/acid: LOW 5,050t gypsum /8,732.5t H2SO4; BASE 28,000t/16,800t; HIGH 55,000t/24,750t. Extreme physical storage case: BASE with *all receipt gates false* produces no eligible agricultural or industrial allocation, accumulates 2.1Mt gypsum over 30 years under unconstrained numerical stock model, **NOT an actionable stockpile**.

For BASE with synthetic national-sulfur AGR cap 10% versus 80%: 30y AGR 80,969t versus 196,525t; possible acid 807,613t versus 761,390t. The cap is GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED, not existing Atlas policy, and essential soil remedies and actual national sulfur needs are to be separately reviewed.

## Physical precursor envelope matters
Independent Ca + SO4 feed limited check, synthetic brine: LOW q90k m³/d, Ca450mg/L, SO4 2800mg/L, 35% limiting-ion recovery -> **22,226t/y gypsum**; BASE q150k, Ca680, SO4 4500, 60% -> **95,962t/y**; HIGH q180k, Ca850, SO4 5500, 75% -> **179,928t/y**. These should not be conflated with the 30k/70k/110k qualified-product allocation sensitivities. In particular BASE physical chemistry hypothetical 95,962t/y exceeds its allocation sensitivity of 70kt; difference could reflect qualification losses but **the link is not physically modeled**. Site flow, actual Ca and SO4 assay, duty cycle, scale control, and quality verification required.

## Accounting and model limitations
At-cost Lattice internal transfer, zero direct production or fiscal credit. No external export authorized. Model has no verified soil maps, multi-class economics, crop yields, freight, hub CAPEX/throughput, actual sulfur trade changes, storage capacity, salinity runoff or waterway residual fates. Its high hectare soil starting inputs 10–30t/ha are **hypothetical one-time remediation range** and do not license application. `acid_t_per_dry_gypsum_t` is a synthetic process ratio, not experimentally demonstrated at Dongjiakou. **No measured Dongjiakou yield impact, H2SO4 output, or sulfur import replacement**.

Output CSVs and scenario JSON generated locally in conversation; commit remains synthetic and distinct from physically verified pilot work. One implementation risk to fix in next version: default source lets indefinite theoretical inventory grow without storage-cost/capacity gates.
